originalBindingCheck.method: Read bytes and SHA-256 locally; historical source-review files bound as files without replaying their reviews or opening any pixels.

footnote.notOwned: No page-63 footnote belongs to this lesson; do not substitute one or infer ownership from a SOURCE60-63 report filename.

structuralExpectations.mathPolicy: Retain every original inline formula token, including bare Cyrillic _м in the emf, voltage and current amplitudes. Do not change math for native label localization.

scientificReviewMethod.basis: Independent reading of immutable original lesson and raw text transcriptions, plus standard physical reasoning; no new online factual research or unverified external replacement facts.
scientificReviewMethod.qualifications: Judge only correctness and source fidelity. Scientifically necessary restrictions may qualify source generalizations, but cannot delete the underlying explanations, historical data, entities or formulas.
scientificReviewMethod.figures: Figure placeholders, captions and textual cross-references are included structurally only. No pixel opening, geometry/arrow/curve assessment, figure semantics or figure approval.
scientificReviewMethod.safety: Historical CRT and mains connection wording must remain descriptive and attributable, not a procedure inviting a learner to connect an instrument directly to live mains.
scientificReviewMethod.scope: Text only; no whole-course, product, figure, publication or finalization approval.

blocks.meaning: Real lossy circuits have decaying free electrical oscillations; maintained forced electrical oscillations have practical importance.
conditions: Rapid decay and inability to use free oscillations must not become universal physical laws; ideal lossless oscillations and other useful transient phenomena are not ruled out.
A persistent driven state needs continued energy input to replace dissipation, not creation of energy without damping.
numbersHistoryEntities: Source contrast: free versus forced electrical oscillations.

blocks.meaning: Lighting and industrial AC exemplify forced electrical oscillations; the chapter models their current as harmonic.
conditions: AC is not defined as necessarily sinusoidal; source sine-law generalization needs its harmonic model.
Do not assert that every contemporary load draws a sinusoidal current; source applications must remain.

blocks.meaning: The source describes a historical electron-beam oscilloscope: voltage acts on vertical deflection plates; a sawtooth-controlled horizontal time sweep yields a sinusoidal trace; calibrated horizontal motion permits frequency inference.
conditions: The mains connection is historical description, not an authorized experiment or direct live-mains hookup instruction.
A repeat period from the calibrated sweep determines cycles per second.
50 Hz means 50 complete cycles each second, containing 50 half-cycle intervals in each direction; not 50 total half-cycles or 100 complete cycles.
The stated observation, many-country industrial 50 Hz and US example 60 Hz must all be explicitly source-attributed, not silently replaced by newly researched current values.
numbersHistoryEntities: Some countries including the United States: source industrial 60 Hz.
Vertical deflection plates, electron beam, experimenter-selected sawtooth frequency and horizontal sweep.

blocks.meaning: Retain the original figure placeholder in position; empty text does not license any figure interpretation.
conditions: Figure remains unapproved and outside visual/semantic review.

blocks.meaning: Caption identifies the electronic oscilloscope and Figure 32; preserve this identification in both languages.
conditions: Caption translation is text-only and does not approve the unseen instrument or waveform.

blocks.meaning: Harmonic applied voltage can produce harmonic electric field and carrier drift; the source relates instantaneous electron drift to instantaneous field and current to circuit voltage, as in DC.
conditions: Distinguish directed drift from total microscopic electron velocity.
Instantaneous proportional drift response is a low-frequency/local ohmic approximation when relaxation is fast compared with the oscillation timescale, not all carriers/materials/frequencies.
Relating terminal voltage to local field requires the circuit approximation addressed next.
Do not extend a resistive in-phase proportionality to arbitrary reactive circuits; circuit properties affect current amplitude and phase.

blocks.meaning: Electrical field changes propagate at finite speed. If propagation time through the circuit is much shorter than the voltage oscillation period, simultaneous changes are a useful approximation; current at the same instant is approximately equal in all cross-sections of an unbranched circuit.
conditions: Preserve finite, not infinite, propagation speed.
Preserve propagation-time much less than period, not just 'fast'.
Current equality is within an unbranched lumped/quasistatic circuit neglecting appreciable distributed charge accumulation/storage and leakage; not a claim of universal instantaneous action.
Retain the source's grade-nine cross-reference as source history if adapted.
numbersHistoryEntities: All circuit cross-sections at one instant.

blocks.meaning: Power-station generators convert mechanical to electrical energy and supply the source's alternating lighting-socket voltage. The simple generator model from Section 17 uses a loop of area S with flux determined by the angle between its chosen normal and magnetic induction.
conditions: For the stated flux expression, use a planar loop in a uniform magnetic field with constant B and S.
Alpha is measured from the area normal, not from the plane of the loop.
Choose a consistent normal/orientation so flux and induced emf are signed quantities.
Do not import an unowned turn-count factor or a different generator model.
numbersHistoryEntities: Power station and lighting socket source context.

blocks.meaning: Retain the second original figure placeholder in position without visual or semantic review.
conditions: Figure remains unapproved.

blocks.meaning: Uniform angular rotation makes the rotation phase advance linearly with time.
conditions: Choose t=0 at alpha=0 to retain the source formula; otherwise an initial phase is needed.
Omega denotes angular rate, not ordinary frequency in Hz.
Angle here is the continuously advancing rotational phase used in cosine, not a bounded unsigned geometrical angle.

blocks.meaning: The rotating-loop flux varies harmonically with time.
conditions: Inherit constant B, S, omega and chosen initial phase from the same generator model.
Do not generalize sinusoidal flux to arbitrary motion or field variation.
numbersHistoryEntities: Same loop and field as blocks 8 and 10.

blocks.meaning: Retain Figure 33 caption and number in both languages, without adding claims about its unseen content.
conditions: Text/number only.

blocks.meaning: Faraday induction gives the oriented emf as the negative time derivative of signed flux; differentiating cosine yields the source's positive sine expression.
conditions: Prime denotes time derivative.
Keep the negative derivative and the positive sine result; consistent boundary orientation corresponds to the selected surface normal.
Retain the same single-loop, uniform field, constant-area/rate model.
Preserve the exact bare Cyrillic amplitude subscript.
numbersHistoryEntities: Source paragraph spanning PDF pages 59 and 60.
Induced emf e, flux Phi, emf amplitude mathcal E.

blocks.meaning: Emf amplitude in the source's rotating-loop model is BS omega.
conditions: B, S and omega are magnitudes/rate in this model, with amplitude nonnegative.
Do not confuse amplitude with RMS value or introduce a turn factor.
Preserve bare Cyrillic _м.

blocks.meaning: The ensuing study concerns forced electromagnetic oscillations under harmonic voltage of angular frequency omega, expressed with sine or cosine.
conditions: This is sinusoidal excitation, not every alternating signal.
The simple same-frequency harmonic response later requires a linear steady-state model, not nonlinear distortion or startup transients.
If frequency conversion is added, omega=2 pi f and f=1/T are distinct from angular frequency.

blocks.meaning: Equation 2.12 defines instantaneous harmonic voltage with a chosen zero initial phase.
conditions: Preserve exact formula and number.
u is instantaneous voltage; U is amplitude, not RMS.
Do not localize bare Cyrillic _м during this phase.

blocks.meaning: U with the source amplitude subscript is voltage amplitude; marker 1 points to the sine/cosine phase footnote.
conditions: Amplitude is peak magnitude, not RMS.
Retain the marker and footnote ownership.

blocks.meaning: The owned footnote says switching sine to cosine shifts voltage initial phase by pi/2 and does not change the substance of the forced-oscillation study.
conditions: This freedom is a consistent time origin/common initial phase choice, not a way to erase physical voltage-current relative phase.
Changing only one physical signal's phase would change their relative phase; both representations must shift consistently.
Preserve footnote as a footnote block, not substitute page 63 material.

blocks.meaning: Harmonic voltage produces a current of the same frequency in the intended driven model, but generally a different phase; the source compares velocity versus driving force in forced mechanical vibration and introduces instantaneous i.
conditions: Correct the source's ordinary 'frequency omega' wording to angular frequency without changing the symbol.
Same-frequency single-sinusoid current is a linear steady-state response after free transients decay, not any arbitrary nonlinear circuit or instant after switching on.
Retain mechanical analogy specifically velocity and force, not displacement and force.
Different voltage/current phases are physical and cannot be dismissed by block 18.
numbersHistoryEntities: Electrical current i at any instant within the stated steady-state model.

blocks.meaning: Equation 2.13 gives instantaneous current with a signed relative phase using the source plus-varphi convention.
conditions: Preserve plus sign, parentheses, equation number and bare Cyrillic _м.
Varphi is the current phase minus voltage phase; do not silently switch to a minus convention.
Do not assert that both currents and voltages always peak together.

blocks.meaning: I with the amplitude subscript is current amplitude; varphi is voltage-current phase difference in the displayed convention.
conditions: Positive varphi means current leads voltage and negative varphi means it lags, modulo whole cycles.
Amplitude is peak magnitude, not RMS.
The phase difference is unchanged by a common change of time origin.
